findings.text: follow-on: _review_owed_fields catches only OSError, so a non-OSError raised inside review_coverage — for example from flight.resolve while resolving the project config — propagates out of _edit_plan_tool after the plan write already succeeded, reporting a completed write as a tool error; catching it and setting review_owed null with review_owed_error, as the OSError branch already does, would keep the write's answer honest.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit — 419571efa renames _review_coverage to review_coverage across reckon/crew/plan_review.py, its read_plan_review caller, the routing.py gate and four test files, adds _review_owed_fields and wires it into _edit_plan_tool, and adds the new test file and the two skill paragraphs; 63a010ea4 adds only the evidence fragment; d185ca050 narrows the predicate's catch from Exception to OSError and reports null review_owed with review_owed_error rather than an empty list, updates both skills and the fragment, and adds the unreadable-coverage test.

item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits 419571efa, 63a010ea4, d185ca050, baseline_suite and after_suite both completed with failure_count 0, negative_control_log names 3 failed EXIT=1; the head arm ran at d185ca050, the reviewed head.

justifications.durability: every done-when clause has a test and the failure path is now covered (tests/test_an_edit_tells_its_author_a_review_is_owed.py:test_an_unreadable_plan_reports_the_review_as_unknown), with the negative control reddening exactly the three done-when cases; the residual is that a non-OSError inside review_coverage would abort a completed write.

justifications.fit: the broad Exception with noqa BLE001 is gone at head in favour of the typed OSError catch (reckon/mcp.py:493), the helper is module-private with a lazy import, and no plan or stage label appears anywhere in the diff.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §26 is met end to end — review_owed lists each uncovered unit with its measured change, is [] when nothing is owed, and is null with review_owed_error when the predicate cannot answer, and the one predicate review_coverage is called by both the gate (reckon/crew/routing.py:2673) and the edit tool (reckon/mcp.py:490), so the two cannot disagree.
justifications.reuse: the node renames the one predicate to review_coverage and updates every caller rather than adding a second reader beside it, and _review_owed_fields only formats its return, so the gate's refusal and the edit's report cannot drift.
